title: Shakshuka
subtitle: with tofu in a spicy tomato sauce
menu_blurb: A rich, spicy tomato, garlic and onion sauce simmered with paprika and cumin, with tender tofu standing in for the traditional poached eggs.
intro: A rich, spicy tomato, garlic and onion sauce, traditionally made with poached eggs. We make a vegan version with tofu. It’s eaten for breakfast or any meal of the day, and it’s made from simple, healthy ingredients. Our first shakshuka was in Israel, and to this day it is still the best we have ever had. A family favorite amongst the Sandlers (à la Noah).
origin: Shakshuka comes from North Africa, most likely Tunisia and the Maghreb, and its name comes from Amazigh (Berber) and Arabic words meaning “all mixed up.” The dish could only develop after tomatoes and chili peppers arrived in North Africa from the Americas in the 16th century. North African Jewish immigrants brought it to Israel in the 1950s, where it became a national staple.

mise_en_place.label: Chop
mise_en_place.task: Mince the garlic, and slice the onion lengthwise, from pole to pole

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A cast iron pan if you have one, or any deep nonstick pan

items.name: Medium firm tofu, cut in medium cubes
Large onion, sliced pole to pole

steps.title: Prepare
instructions: Slice the onion lengthwise, from pole to pole.

steps.title: Build the sauce
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in the pan and cook the onion for about 5 minutes, until halfway cooked.
Add the garlic and the spices and cook until nice and fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Taste and season with more salt and pepper as needed.

steps.title: Add the tofu
instructions: Add the tofu cubes to the sauce and let them warm through.

steps.title: Serve
instructions: Serve in small bowls, sprinkled with chopped parsley.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more spicy paprika for an extra kick.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Add spinach, eggplant, and/or peppers to the sauce. For the traditional version, make small wells in the sauce, crack 6 to 8 eggs into them, and cook (covered speeds it up) for about 15 minutes until poached.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keeps for a few days in the fridge, but it is best eaten fresh.

notebook.question: What is tofu, and is it good for you?
answer: Tofu is a nutrient-dense, plant-based protein made from curdled soy milk pressed into blocks. It is low in calories, has zero cholesterol, and is a complete protein with all nine essential amino acids your body can’t make on its own.
Its nutrition varies with firmness. Firmer varieties hold less water, so they carry more protein, fat, and calories per serving.

table.label: Extra firm
table.text: 15 to 17 g protein and about 145 calories

table.label: Firm
table.text: 8 to 10 g protein and 70 to 80 calories

table.label: Silken or soft
table.text: About 4 to 7 g protein and 40 to 62 calories

benefits.label: Heart health
benefits.text: Cholesterol-free and low in saturated fat, tofu may help reduce LDL cholesterol. Studies show eating at least one serving a week may lower heart disease risk by 18%.

benefits.label: Nutrient-rich
benefits.text: A good source of iron, manganese, selenium, phosphorus, and calcium, especially when made with calcium sulfate.

benefits.label: Cancer risk reduction
benefits.text: Tofu contains isoflavones, with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and potential protective effects against breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers.

benefits.label: Bone health
benefits.text: Its high calcium and magnesium content helps prevent osteoporosis.

notebook.question: Are soy products good for you?
answer: Generally, yes. Soy is a nutrient-dense, plant-based protein that can lower cholesterol and reduce heart disease risk. Whole soy foods like tofu, edamame, and tempeh are packed with isoflavones and fiber, making them a healthy alternative to red meat.
